# Design brief — chart-first demo v0.1

## Goal

Deliver one convincing demo:

> Open 10 September 2026 → see the real Panchavati compact chart → edit a staff assignment → save to PostgreSQL → reload → see the change persisted → print the same six-sheet chart.

Everything else is secondary.

## Demo route

To avoid breaking the already-working print renderer:

```text
React demo screen:
  /app/charts/2026-09-10

Existing server-rendered/print path:
  /charts/2026-09-10
```

Once React matches the current renderer, we can make React the default screen route. The existing server renderer remains the print/PDF authority during this milestone.

## UI structure

### Top navigation

Use Kushal's grouped navigation style, without the chart-type/profile dropdown:

```text
Dashboard
दैनिक कर्तव्य तक्ते
  └── पंचवटी तक्ता
      ├── पृष्ठ १: दैनिक कर्तव्य तक्ता
      ├── पृष्ठ २: रात्रपाळी कर्तव्य
      ├── पृष्ठ ३: रजा व विशेष कर्तव्य
      ├── पृष्ठ ४: मनुष्यबळ तक्ता
      ├── पृष्ठ ५: पोलीस अधिकारी
      └── पृष्ठ ६: गस्त व स्कॅनिंग

कार्यवाही
  ├── कार्यकारी डॅशबोर्ड
  ├── कर्तव्य फलक
  ├── बंदोबस्त व विशेष मोहीम
  └── ऐतिहासिक शोध

डेटा
  ├── मास्टर डेटा
  └── दस्तऐवज आयात / OCR
```

Only the real demo route is enabled initially. Other unfinished routes are disabled and labelled `Coming Soon`.

### Chart screen

The chart itself must not become a dashboard.

Use:

- compact-v3 page grammar;
- same navy/white/blue/red/yellow semantics;
- same six logical sections;
- same low-noise table layout;
- no decorative cards around chart content;
- no unnecessary KPI blocks;
- no chart-type selector;
- no horizontal page overflow;
- Marathi wraps instead of truncating.

React components should reuse the existing class vocabulary and visual baseline from:

```text
design/compv3.css
design/panchavati-compv3.html
```

## React architecture

```text
PostgreSQL
  ↓
Fastify API
  ↓
ChartDocument
  ↓
React screen + authoring
  ↓
existing server renderer → print/PDF
```

React must not query PostgreSQL directly and must not reimplement domain rules.

The React client will initially consume:

```text
GET  /api/charts/:date
PATCH /api/charts/:date/assignments/:id
GET  /api/masters
```

Existing label, chowki, officer-box, finalize and reopen APIs remain available and are not redesigned during this first slice.

## First editing interactions

Only implement the smallest real authoring flow first:

1. Click a person or vacant slot.
2. Open staff picker.
3. Search by Marathi name, English name, buckle number or rank.
4. Select a staff member.
5. Persist through PostgreSQL.
6. Reload and verify the assignment remains.
7. Clear the slot back to `रिक्त`.
8. Toggle explicit `बिमा` where applicable.
9. Show save/error state honestly.

The clerk remains the only decision-maker. No auto-fill, replacement suggestion or smart scheduling.

## Database

No new migration is needed for this first React slice.

Use the already-clean baseline:

- `panchavati3_dev`;
- `panchavati3_test`;
- 10/09 DRAFT chart;
- 179 staff;
- 212 assignment rows;
- 77 tests currently green.

Do not reset or reseed again unless a concrete problem requires it.

## Source work

Do not spend the next pass on a complete OCR/staff-count research project.

Before implementation, perform only a narrow source sanity check for the demo:

- title/date;
- 10/09 page count;
- `बिमा`, `रिक्त`, `बंद`;
- major chowki names;
- protected English tokens;
- obvious name/spelling risks;
- no-loss count.

The full 10/09/11/Staff_Info comparison can happen after the demo is functional.

## Explicitly deferred

Not part of this implementation slice:

- 11/09 event annex;
- legacy six-page viewer;
- OCR import;
- full historical search;
- real authentication migration;
- full master-data CRUD;
- complete leave/manpower/notice/event authoring;
- multi-station support;
- WhatsApp/Telegram/cloud integrations;
- full template builder.

Real auth is only planned for later. The current local pseudo-login remains active.

## Demo acceptance criteria

The slice is successful when:

- React screen opens with the real 10/09 chart;
- compact-v3 chart content is visible and readable;
- no major page-level horizontal overflow exists;
- the chart has no missing assignment rows;
- a staff assignment can be changed through the UI;
- the change survives reload;
- clearing creates `रिक्त`;
- BIMA remains an explicit per-assignment field;
- existing `npm run check` remains green;
- existing `npm run print:audit` remains 6/6;
- print output is unchanged by the React migration.

I will not begin implementation until you approve this brief. Reply **“GO with this design”** and I’ll implement the smallest vertical slice first.

You’re right. I was still reasoning internally instead of giving you the actual revised design output. No implementation has started. Here is the corrected design brief based on your feedback.

# Compact-v4 design brief, revised

## Core correction

We are **not** trying to recreate the old six-page chart.

We are designing a new compact chart that:

- preserves the useful first-page structure suggested by SPI sir;
- keeps the main officer hierarchy visually prominent;
- shows day and night side by side where their structures genuinely match;
- uses six or seven sheets maximum;
- carries all real 10/09 information;
- is more space-efficient than the original;
- avoids the long horizontal standardized chart problem;
- avoids dashboard cards and decorative UI;
- remains editable through efficient contextual CRUD.

The old six-page chart will exist inside the application as:

```text
Legacy Panchavati Chart
Reference only
Coming Soon / WIP
```

It will not be the active design target.

---

# 1. Persistent application header

The header should be persistent across the application and not change from page to page.

## Main header contains navigation only

It should not contain:

- DRAFT;
- FINALIZED;
- Edit;
- Finalize;
- Print;
- page-specific chart actions.

Those belong in a second, page-specific toolbar.

## Proposed persistent header

### Left side

```text
[Police logo]

महाराष्ट्र पोलीस
पंचवटी पोलीस ठाणे
नाशिक शहर | Panchavati Police Station
```

Then:

```text
Daily Duty Chart
```

or Marathi equivalent, controlled by the language toggle.

Do not display both English and Marathi versions simultaneously.

### Language behavior

A navbar language toggle changes interface labels:

```text
मराठी | English
```

When Marathi is selected:

```text
दैनिक कर्तव्य तक्ता
कार्यवाही
मास्टर डेटा
ऐतिहासिक शोध
```

When English is selected:

```text
Daily Duty Chart
Operations
Master Data
Historical Search
```

Identity values and source operational wording remain source-preserved unless specifically designed for translation.

The chart's official Marathi output remains Marathi-first. The UI language toggle should not silently translate police names, source notes, rank codes or protected terms.

## Right side

Use a richer date selector inspired by Kushal and Arjish:

- current selected date;
- Marathi weekday in Marathi mode;
- Today;
- Tomorrow;
- Previous/next available chart;
- chart availability indicator;
- calendar picker;
- search existing dates;
- amendment/version indicator where relevant.

No chart-format/profile dropdown.

## Navigation structure

Use the useful grouped structure from Kushal's AppNav, but simplify the labels and remove scrapped legacy items.

```text
डॅशबोर्ड

दैनिक कर्तव्य तक्ते
  पंचवटी तक्ता
    मुख्य तक्ता
    रात्रपाळी व सूचना
    रजा व विशेष कर्तव्य
    मनुष्यबळ
    अधिकारी सारांश
    गस्त व स्कॅनिंग

कार्यवाही
  कार्यकारी आढावा
  कर्तव्य फलक
  बंदोबस्त व विशेष मोहीम
  ऐतिहासिक शोध

डेटा
  मास्टर डेटा
  दस्तऐवज आयात
  जुना पंचवटी तक्ता
```

The following can be visible but disabled:

```text
बंदोबस्त व विशेष मोहीम     Coming Soon
ऐतिहासिक शोध               Coming Soon
दस्तऐवज आयात               Coming Soon
जुना पंचवटी तक्ता           Reference / WIP
Master Data                 Partial / WIP
```

This lets the user see what the product is becoming without pretending those features work.

---

# 2. Page-specific chart toolbar

Below the persistent header, the chart route gets its own compact toolbar.

Example:

```text
पंचवटी दैनिक कर्तव्य तक्ता
१०/०९/२०२६ · गुरुवार

DRAFT
संपादन
अंतिम करा
प्रिंट
```

The toolbar should not use goofy emoji icons.

Use text buttons with restrained symbols only where useful:

```text
संपादन
अंतिम करा
प्रिंट
अधिक
```

Possible minimal icons:

- calendar icon for date;
- pencil icon only if it is visually consistent;
- printer icon only if it improves recognition.

Do not write:

```text
✏️ संपादन (Edit Mode)
✅ अंतिम करा (Finalize)
🖨 प्रिंट / PDF (A4)
```

That is visually noisy and duplicates the language.

## Lifecycle behavior

The hard historical rule must remain:

```text
DRAFT → VALIDATED → FINALIZED
```

A finalized version must remain immutable.

For the clerk, the experience can still feel reversible:

```text
DRAFT
  → अंतिम करा
FINALIZED
  → सुधारणा सुरू करा
नवीन सुधारणा मसुदा
```

“सुधारणा सुरू करा” creates a new amendment draft. It does not mutate the old finalized chart.

The visible status may show:

```text
FINALIZED · आवृत्ती १
सुधारणा मसुदा · आवृत्ती २
```

If the clerk wants to change something after finalization:

1. click `सुधारणा सुरू करा`;
2. system creates a new draft version;
3. original finalized version remains available;
4. clerk edits the amendment;
5. clerk finalizes the new version.

This is safer and follows the existing domain contract.

---

# 3. Page 1 design

Your correction is right. The main officer arrangement should remain.

SPI sir specifically suggested:

1. senior officer above;
2. four subordinate officer areas below;
3. day/night duty areas below them.

That is not the old standardized chart. It is a distinct command-oriented hierarchy and should remain.

## Page 1 structure

```text
Persistent app header
Page toolbar

Panchavati Police Station, Nashik City
Daily Duty Chart
Date · weekday

Senior officer command block

Four subordinate officer blocks

Day shift                  Night shift
```

## Senior officer block

Centered, but compact.

```text
वपोनि गजेंद्र पाटील
ठाणे प्रमुख
```

Below it:

```text
रायटर
पोहवा १३४७ जाधव

चालक
दिवस       ...
रात्र       ...
```

If no data exists for a field, show a clean empty state rather than a fake placeholder.

## Four officer blocks

Keep four horizontally aligned officer blocks.

They should be shorter and more structured than the current mock.

### Example

```text
पोनि सुनिल पवार
क्राईम

रायटर
...

RTPC
दिवस    ...
रात्र    ...

ऑपरेटर
दिवस    ...
रात्र    ...
```

The four blocks can use a shared compact grid:

```text
[Officer 1] [Officer 2] [Officer 3] [Officer 4]
```

Do not make them tall dashboard cards.

### Important data honesty

At present, the available Panchavati data does not establish complete officer-to-writer, RTPC and operator mappings for every officer.

Therefore:

- show only source-backed relationships;
- leave unsupported fields blank or explicitly unavailable;
- do not invent RTPC/operator assignments;
- keep the CRUD model ready for future additions;
- add an officer box through a real blank slot, as the current implementation already does.

## Rank tooltip

The rank abbreviation tooltip should not appear below the text or cause reflow.

Better behavior:

- on hover or keyboard focus;
- position in a fixed top-right tooltip layer;
- single line where possible;
- no layout movement;
- disappears on mouse exit;
- hidden in print.

Example:

```text
पोनि
```

Tooltip:

```text
पोलीस निरीक्षक
```

No inline `abbr` expansion that shifts the row.

---

# 4. Day and night structure

Your correction is important.

Night is **not** a completely different data model.

For the first three columns, day and night follow nearly the same broad grouping:

```text
Station and internal units
Chowkis
Marshal and special posts
```

The major difference is the fourth column:

- day includes office/clerical/special duty groupings;
- night includes instructions/notices and night-specific directives.

Therefore Page 1 should preserve the side-by-side visual comparison:

```text
दिवसपाळी                         रात्रपाळी
०९:०० ते २१:००                   २१:०० ते ०९:००
```

The shared group ordering should remain aligned as much as possible:

```text
ठाणे / वरिष्ठ अधिकारी       ठाणे / वरिष्ठ अधिकारी
ठाणे अंमलदार                ठाणे अंमलदार
हजरपाळी                     हजरपाळी
CCTNS                        CCTNS
वायरलेस                     वायरलेस
पिटर मोबाईल                 पिटर मोबाईल
सी.आर. मोबाईल               सी.आर. मोबाईल
DB                           DB
लॉकअप                       लॉकअप
```

This makes comparison fast for a daily clerk.

## Row compression

Do not show every staff member as a large isolated table row with repeated labels.

Use grouped row spans:

```text
ठाणे अंमलदार
  पोहवा १४५२ लांडे

हजरपाळी
  पोशि २५७१ देशमुख
  पोशि २०८९ कदम
```

The role label occupies one narrow left column. People occupy the larger right column.

Where day and night are side by side, use equivalent widths:

```text
role | staff                         role | staff
```

Do not use four oversized cards around these tables.

---

# 5. What moves away from Page 1

You were right that putting both:

```text
कार्यालयीन शाखा व कारकून
कोर्ट, समन्स, वॉरंट व विशेष कक्ष
```

on Page 1 creates overload.

They should move to the next logical sheet with the office/special content.

## Proposed distribution

### Page 1

- senior officer;
- four officer blocks;
- day shift core;
- night shift core;
- only the high-priority shared station/chowki command information.

### Page 2

- office/clerical branches;
- court;
- summons;
- warrants;
- special desks;
- marshal/special posts;
- night instructions;
- notices where necessary.

### Page 3

- six chowkis in the compact 3×2 matrix;
- day/night paired chowki rows;
- marshal lines;
- `बंद` and `चार्ज`;
- BIMA assignments.

This lets Page 1 remain visually strong without dropping content.

It also avoids returning to the old standardized format because we are not placing everything in one long horizontal mega-table. We are using multiple deliberate sheets with better grouping.

---

# 6. Target physical sheet count

The target should be:

```text
Normal day: 5 or 6 sheets
Dense/event day: 6 or 7 sheets
Never more than the original packet without a clear reason
```

The first acceptance target is:

- 10/09: no more than 6 sheets if readable;
- 11/09: no more than 7 sheets because of the event annex;
- no information loss;
- no tiny unreadable text;
- no massive empty spaces.

If a real 10/09 chart needs six sheets, that is acceptable. The improvement must come from:

- better grouping;
- less border noise;
- more useful horizontal allocation;
- fewer repeated labels;
- reduced whitespace;
- faster scanning;
- cleaner editing.

Not merely from forcing it into fewer pages.

---

# 7. Office and special content sheet

The office and court content should be represented as dense branch tables, not cards.

Example:

```text
कार्यालयीन शाखा व कारकून

शाखा                         कर्मचारी
कार्यालयीन अंमलदार           ...
प्रशासन रायटर                ...
तपास रायटर                  ...
नगदी कारकून                  रिक्त
मुद्देमाल कारकून             ...
गोपनीय ड्युटी                ...
हजेरी मास्तर                 ...
क्राईम कारकून                ...
बारनिशी                      ...
MOB / मिसिंग                 ...
वॉरंट                        ...
```

Then:

```text
कोर्ट, समन्स, वॉरंट व विशेष कक्ष

कर्तव्य                       दिवसपाळी              रात्रपाळी
कोर्ट पैरवी                   ...                    ...
समन्स                         ...                    ...
वॉरंट                         ...                    ...
सायबर सेल                    ...                    ...
महिला कक्ष                   ...                    ...
काळाराम मंदीर गार्ड          ...                    ...
```

This is more efficient than one card for each office role.

Use:

- a single section heading;
- thin horizontal rules;
- role grouping;
- no nested rounded boxes.

---

# 8. CRUD design

The existing three-option workflow should remain and be improved rather than replaced.

When a clerk clicks an assignment, open a centered viewport-safe editor.

## Popup layout

The popup should be:

- centered;
- maximum height around 80–85vh;
- internally scrollable only when necessary;
- wide enough for search and details;
- symmetric;
- keyboard accessible;
- closable with Escape and outside click;
- not require repeated navigation to Master Data.

### Header

```text
कर्मचारी नेमणूक
काटया मारूती · दिवसपाळी
```

### Current assignment panel

```text
सध्याचा कर्मचारी
पोशि ५४२ आहेर
```

Actions:

```text
कर्मचारी माहिती बदला
रिक्त करा
बिमा
```

### Main three options

#### 1. Current master details

```text
कर्मचारी माहिती बदला
```

Opens an inline edit section:

```text
नाव मराठीत
नाव इंग्रजीत
हुद्दा
बकल नंबर
फोन

[जतन करा] [रद्द]
```

This edits the master record and clearly warns:

```text

Daily Duty Chart
```

or Marathi equivalent, controlled by the language toggle.

Do not display both English and Marathi versions simultaneously.


Traps that cost time before — do not rediscover them:

1. **`npm run start|dev` has no watch for the renderer.** Editing `server/**` requires a server
   restart (`netstat -ano | grep :3100` → `taskkill //PID <pid> //T //F`), otherwise you debug stale HTML.
2. **Preview screenshots are intermittent** ("webview is not being composited"). Reload/reopen the tab
   and retry; for anything precise prefer DOM measurements (`preview_evaluate`) or `npm run print:audit`.
3. **`code_search`/ripgrep is broken** in this environment (`ENOENT … rg.exe`). Use `grep -n` via the
   terminal, or Python for Unicode-aware scans.
4. **Chrome CLI needs a Windows path**: `--print-to-pdf="$(cygpath -w …)"`; binary at
   `C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe` (`CHROME_PATH` overrides).
5. **Invariant 5 scans `db/`, `server/`, `scripts/` for any `fetch(`/axios.** A new dev tool that talks
   HTTP goes in **`tools/`** (that is why `tools/print-audit.mjs` lives there) — never weaken the scan.
6. **`authoring.css` applies on screen *and* in print**; only its `@media print` blocks are print-only.
   `compv3.css` is human-owned: authoring/density/defect fixes go in `authoring.css`.
7. Pages are A4 **landscape**: `.page` = 1122×794 px, `@page margin 0`, print padding 5mm.

- `daily_charts(chart_id, chart_date, lifecycle DRAFT|VALIDATED|FINALIZED, template_version_id,
  presentation_overrides jsonb)` — overrides live here.
- `daily_assignments(chart_id, shift DAY|NIGHT, duty_id, duty_title_mr, location_id, staff_id,
  allocation_state ALLOCATED|VACANT_RIKT, is_bima, role_mr, start_time, end_time, notes_mr, sort_order,
  column_no)` — `column_no` is the source duty-column identity (1 staff desks / 2 chowkis /
  3 marshal+specials / 4 office+court / 5 notices).
- `locations(kind STATION|CHOWKI|MARSHAL_POST|OFFICE|COURT|FIXED_POINT)`; marshal/desk folding config is
  **template display config**, not data: `template_versions.layout.marshalPostForChowki`,
  `.specialDeskLocationKinds`, `.courtDutyCodes`, `.officerBoxes`, `.matrixColumns`,
  `.availabilitySections`, `.scanSessions`.
- Ranks (`rank_code`, `short_form_mr`, `cadre`): OFFICER = SR_PI वपोनि, PI पोनि, API सपोनि, PSI पोउनि,
  PROB_PSI परि.पोउनि, PROB_LPSI परि.मपोउनि, GRADE_PSI ग्रेपोउनि; CONSTABULARY = ASI सपोउनि, LASI मसपोउनि,
  HC पोहवा, DRIVER_HC चापोहवा, LHC मपोहवा, PN पोना, PC पोशि, DRIVER_PC चापोशि, LPC मपोशि; HOME_GUARD होम.
- Three facts never blur: `रिक्त` (VACANT_RIKT slot) ≠ `बंद` (location state) ≠ `बिमा` (explicit boolean).

Persistent application header The header should be persistent across the application and not change from page to page. ## Main header contains navigation only It should not contain: - DRAFT; - FINALIZED; - Edit; - Finalize; - Print; - page-specific chart actions. Those belong in a second, page-specific toolbar. ## Proposed persistent header ### Left side ```text [Police logo] महाराष्ट्र पोलीस पंचवटी पोलीस ठाणे नाशिक शहर | Panchavati Police Station ``` Then: ```text Daily Duty Chart ``` or Marathi equivalent, controlled by the language toggle. Do not display both English and Marathi versions simultaneously. ### Language behavior A navbar language toggle changes interface labels: ```text मराठी | English ``` When Marathi is selected: ```text दैनिक कर्तव्य तक्ता कार्यवाही मास्टर डेटा ऐतिहासिक शोध ``` When English is selected: ```text Daily Duty Chart Operations Master Data Historical Search ``` Identity values and source operational wording remain source-preserved unless specifically designed for translation. The chart's official Marathi output remains Marathi-first. The UI language toggle should not silently translate police names, source notes, rank codes or protected terms. ## Right side Use a richer date selector inspired by Kushal and Arjish: - current selected date; - Marathi weekday in Marathi mode; - Today; - Tomorrow; - Previous/next available chart; - chart availability indicator; - calendar picker; - search existing dates; - amendment/version indicator where relevant. No chart-format/profile dropdown. ## Navigation structure Use the useful grouped structure from Kushal's AppNav, but simplify the labels and remove scrapped legacy items. ```text डॅशबोर्ड दैनिक कर्तव्य तक्ते पंचवटी तक्ता मुख्य तक्ता रात्रपाळी व सूचना रजा व विशेष कर्तव्य मनुष्यबळ अधिकारी सारांश गस्त व स्कॅनिंग कार्यवाही कार्यकारी आढावा कर्तव्य फलक बंदोबस्त व विशेष मोहीम ऐतिहासिक शोध डेटा मास्टर डेटा दस्तऐवज आयात जुना पंचवटी तक्ता ``` The following can be visible but disabled: ```text बंदोबस्त व विशेष मोहीम Coming Soon ऐतिहासिक शोध Coming Soon दस्तऐवज आयात Coming Soon जुना पंचवटी तक्ता Reference / WIP Master Data Partial / WIP ``` This lets the user see what the product is becoming without pretending those features work. --- # 2. Page-specific chart toolbar Below the persistent header, the chart route gets its own compact toolbar. Example: ```text पंचवटी दैनिक कर्तव्य तक्ता १०/०९/२०२६ · गुरुवार DRAFT संपादन अंतिम करा प्रिंट ``` The toolbar should not use goofy emoji icons. Use text buttons with restrained symbols only where useful: ```text संपादन अंतिम करा प्रिंट अधिक ``` Possible minimal icons: - calendar icon for date; - pencil icon only if it is visually consistent; - printer icon only if it improves recognition. Do not write: ```text ✏️ संपादन (Edit Mode) ✅ अंतिम करा (Finalize) 🖨 प्रिंट / PDF (A4) ``` That is visually noisy and duplicates the language. ## Lifecycle behavior The hard historical rule must remain: ```text DRAFT → VALIDATED → FINALIZED ``` A finalized version must remain immutable. For the clerk, the experience can still feel reversible: ```text DRAFT → अंतिम करा FINALIZED → सुधारणा सुरू करा नवीन सुधारणा मसुदा ``` “सुधारणा सुरू करा” creates a new amendment draft. It does not mutate the old finalized chart. The visible status may show: ```text FINALIZED · आवृत्ती १ सुधारणा मसुदा · आवृत्ती २ ``` If the clerk wants to change something after finalization: 1. click `सुधारणा सुरू करा`; 2. system creates a new draft version; 3. original finalized version remains available; 4. clerk edits the amendment; 5. clerk finalizes the new version. This is safer and follows the existing domain contract. --- # 3. Page 1 design Your correction is right. The main officer arrangement should remain. SPI sir specifically suggested: 1. senior officer above; 2. four subordinate officer areas below; 3. day/night duty areas below them. That is not the old standardized chart. It is a distinct command-oriented hierarchy and should remain. ## Page 1 structure ```text Persistent app header Page toolbar Panchavati Police Station, Nashik City Daily Duty Chart Date · weekday Senior officer command block Four subordinate officer blocks Day shift Night shift ``` ## Senior officer block Centered, but compact. ```text वपोनि गजेंद्र पाटील ठाणे प्रमुख ``` Below it: ```text रायटर पोहवा १३४७ जाधव चालक दिवस ... रात्र ... ``` If no data exists for a field, show a clean empty state rather than a fake placeholder. ## Four officer blocks Keep four horizontally aligned officer blocks. They should be shorter and more structured than the current mock. ### Example ```text पोनि सुनिल पवार क्राईम रायटर ... RTPC दिवस ... रात्र ... ऑपरेटर दिवस ... रात्र ... ``` The four blocks can use a shared compact grid: ```text [Officer 1] [Officer 2] [Officer 3] [Officer 4] ``` Do not make them tall dashboard cards. ### Important data honesty At present, the available Panchavati data does not establish complete officer-to-writer, RTPC and operator mappings for every officer. Better behavior: - on hover or keyboard focus; - position in a fixed top-right tooltip layer; - single line where possible; - no layout movement; - disappears on mouse exit; - hidden in print. Example: ```text पोनि ``` Tooltip: ```text पोलीस निरीक्षक ``` No inline `abbr` expansion that shifts the row. --- # 4. Day and night structure Your correction is important. Night is **not** a completely different data model. For the first three columns, day and night follow nearly the same broad grouping: ```text Station and internal units Chowkis Marshal and special posts ``` The major difference is the fourth column: - day includes office/clerical/special duty groupings; - night includes instructions/notices and night-specific directives. Therefore Page 1 should preserve the side-by-side visual comparison: ```text दिवसपाळी रात्रपाळी ०९:०० ते २१:०० २१:०० ते ०९:०० ``` The shared group ordering should remain aligned as much as possible: ```text ठाणे / वरिष्ठ अधिकारी ठाणे / वरिष्ठ अधिकारी ठाणे अंमलदार ठाणे अंमलदार हजरपाळी हजरपाळी CCTNS CCTNS वायरलेस वायरलेस पिटर मोबाईल पिटर मोबाईल सी.आर. मोबाईल सी.आर. मोबाईल DB DB लॉकअप लॉकअप ``` This makes comparison fast for a daily clerk. ## Row compression Do not show every staff member as a large isolated table row with repeated labels. Use grouped row spans: ```text ठाणे अंमलदार पोहवा १४५२ लांडे हजरपाळी पोशि २५७१ देशमुख पोशि २०८९ कदम ``` The role label occupies one narrow left column. People occupy the larger right column. Where day and night are side by side, use equivalent widths: ```text role | staff role | staff ``` Do not use four oversized cards around these tables. --- # 5. What moves away from Page 1 You were right that putting both: ```text कार्यालयीन शाखा व कारकून कोर्ट, समन्स, वॉरंट व विशेष कक्ष ``` on Page 1 creates overload. They should move to the next logical sheet with the office/special content. ## Proposed distribution ### Page 1 - senior officer; - four officer blocks; - day shift core; - night shift core; - only the high-priority shared station/chowki command information. ### Page 2 - office/clerical branches; - court; - summons; - warrants; - special desks; - marshal/special posts; - night instructions; - notices where necessary. ### Page 3 - six chowkis in the compact 3×2 matrix; - day/night paired chowki rows; - marshal lines; - `बंद` and `चार्ज`; - BIMA assignments. This lets Page 1 remain visually strong without dropping content. It also avoids returning to the old standardized format because we are not placing everything in one long horizontal mega-table. We are using multiple deliberate sheets with better grouping. --- # 6. Target physical sheet count The target should be: ```text Normal day: 5 or 6 sheets Dense/event day: 6 or 7 sheets Never more than the original packet without a clear reason ``` The first acceptance target is: - 10/09: no more than 6 sheets if readable; - 11/09: no more than 7 sheets because of the event annex; - no information loss; - no tiny unreadable text; - no massive empty spaces. Not merely from forcing it into fewer pages. --- # 7. Office and special content sheet The office and court content should be represented as dense branch tables, not cards. Example: ```text कार्यालयीन शाखा व कारकून शाखा कर्मचारी कार्यालयीन अंमलदार ... प्रशासन रायटर ... तपास रायटर ... नगदी कारकून रिक्त मुद्देमाल कारकून ... गोपनीय ड्युटी ... हजेरी मास्तर ... क्राईम कारकून ... बारनिशी ... MOB / मिसिंग ... वॉरंट ... ``` Then: ```text कोर्ट, समन्स, वॉरंट व विशेष कक्ष कर्तव्य दिवसपाळी रात्रपाळी कोर्ट पैरवी ... ... समन्स ... ... वॉरंट ... ... सायबर सेल ... ... महिला कक्ष ... ... काळाराम मंदीर गार्ड ... ... ``` This is more efficient than one card for each office role. Use: - a single section heading; - thin horizontal rules; - role grouping; - no nested rounded boxes. --- # 8. CRUD design The existing three-option workflow should remain and be improved rather than replaced. When a clerk clicks an assignment, open a centered viewport-safe editor. ## Popup layout The popup should be: - centered; - maximum height around 80–85vh; - internally scrollable only when necessary; - wide enough for search and details; - symmetric; - keyboard accessible; - closable with Escape and outside click; - not require repeated navigation to Master Data. ### Header ```text कर्मचारी नेमणूक काटया मारूती · दिवसपाळी ``` ### Current assignment panel ```text सध्याचा कर्मचारी पोशि ५४२ आहेर ``` Actions: ```text कर्मचारी माहिती बदला रिक्त करा बिमा ``` ### Main three options #### 1. Current master details ```text कर्मचारी माहिती बदला ``` Opens an inline edit section: ```text नाव मराठीत नाव इंग्रजीत हुद्दा बकल नंबर फोन [जतन करा] [रद्द] ``` This edits the master record and clearly warns: ```text ही माहिती मास्टर रोस्टरमध्ये बदलेल ``` It should not require opening a separate page. #### 2. Select existing staff Search field: ```text नाव, बकल नंबर किंवा हुद्दा शोधा ``` Results should show: ```text पोशि ५४२ आहेर पोशि १९९८ वाकचैरे पोहवा ६९२ गुंबाडे ``` Each result can include a small secondary availability warning: ```text रजेची नोंद आहे ``` But the system must not block or auto-replace unless a separately approved rule exists. #### 3. Add new staff Inline compact form: ```text नाव मराठीत नाव इंग्रजीत हुद्दा बकल नंबर फोन ``` Action: ```text जतन करून येथे नेमा ``` This creates the master staff record and assigns it to the exact clicked slot. ## Popup footer ```text बंद करा ``` After a successful save: ```text जतन झाले ``` Then reload the relevant ChartDocument. No fake visual-only changes. ## Assignment-specific fields Keep these in the same popup under a compact “या नेमणुकीसाठी” area: ```text वेळ बिमा नोंद ``` Do not mix master fields with assignment fields. That distinction is important: - name/rank/buckle belongs to the staff master; - BIMA/time/role/notes belongs to this chart assignment. --- # 9. Lifecycle and finalization The UI can make the workflow simple: ```text DRAFT संपादन अंतिम करा ``` After finalization: ```text FINALIZED सुधारणा सुरू करा प्रिंट ``` But technically: - finalization creates an immutable snapshot; - “सुधारणा सुरू करा” creates a new amendment draft; - the original final version stays unchanged; - the new draft can be edited and finalized separately. The status label at the top of each chart sheet can remain: ```text DRAFT FINALIZED · आवृत्ती १ सुधारणा मसुदा · आवृत्ती २ ``` The persistent application header itself should not carry this chart-specific state. --- # 10. What we should theoretically verify before implementation No code or mock should be changed yet. We should compare three models using actual 10/09 data: 1. Original six-page reference; 2. current compv3 with full 10/09 data; 3. Compact-v4 proposal above. Acceptance: - 212/212 assignments represented; - no Marathi truncation; - no page-level horizontal overflow; - no unnecessary chart cards; - no fake officer/operator/RTPC data; - no more than six sheets for 10/09 if readability remains acceptable; - no more than seven for 11/09 with the event annex; - first page retains the senior officer plus four-officer hierarchy; - day/night shared structure remains visually comparable; - office/court content no longer overloads Page 1; - CRUD popup handles edit master, select existing and create new without navigating away. ## Important correction to my previous recommendation I previously said not to start React yet. That remains correct, but for a sharper reason: > We must first freeze the Compact-v4 visual grammar against the full 10/09 data. React should implement the approved grammar, not become another place where we discover the design. No implementation has happened yet. The legacy six-page chart should remain a **reference/comparison artifact**. The real design target is an honest upgrade over it, starting from `compv3`. # Design brief: Compact-v4 direction ## 1. Honest verdict on the current mock ### What the mock gets right `design/panchavati-compv3.html` is a strong starting point because it already has: - a chart-like document grammar instead of a dashboard; - low-noise navy/white/slate palette; - compact row-based staff display; - a useful command header; - a reasonable page-1 hierarchy; - a good six-chowki matrix direction; - separate leave, manpower, officer and scan information; - explicit visual distinctions for `रिक्त`, `बंद` and `बिमा`; - no dependency on the old six-page visual structure. ### What is not yet good enough The mock was designed with representative/sample data, so it looks more efficient than it is under the full 10/09 data volume. Main issues: 1. **Page 1 is overloaded** - Sr-PI; - officer boxes; - day deployment; - night deployment; - office; - court/special desk; - several long role groups. It becomes vertically excessive once real source rows are inserted. 2. **The officer boxes consume too much vertical space** - They are useful as a concept. - Their current box treatment creates repeated borders and empty padding. - They should become a compact command strip or a tight officer matrix, not dashboard-like cards. 3. **Every block feels boxed** - The outer table border; - block border; - sub-table border; - row border; - chip border. That produces the “double border / clutter / AI-generated admin UI” feeling you dislike. 4. **Page 3 has uneven density** - One long leave list can force neighbouring columns to leave large empty areas. - The current card/grid approach wastes space when categories have very different lengths. 5. **The mock has a dangerous page-fit illusion** - Sample data fits. - Real 10/09 data does not fit at the same comfortable scale. - We must optimize against maximum realistic source density, not against the sample screenshot. 6. **Page count should not be the optimization target** - Four tiny unreadable pages are worse than six well-packed pages. - The goal is maximum usable information per area without making Marathi difficult to read. ## 2. Core visual principle The new chart should be: > **A clean command document composed of horizontal bands and disciplined columns — not a collection of cards.** ### Remove from the chart itself - rounded cards; - shadows; - decorative pills; - unnecessary nested borders; - large empty card padding; - dashboard KPI tiles; - oversized section headers; - repeated page headers taking excessive height; - labels repeated in every staff row; - full names repeated everywhere. ### Keep - one page frame; - thin section rules; - restrained table gridlines; - clear section bands; - compact source-faithful grouping; - text-based state labels; - small color accents; - full data available through hover/detail editing. --- # 3. Proposed chart grammar ## Outer page Each printed sheet should have: 1. a compact 1-line identity header; 2. a thin date/status line; 3. two to four horizontal content bands; 4. no card shadow; 5. one consistent page border or no border, not several nested frames. ### Header target ```text पंचवटी पोलीस ठाणे, नाशिक शहर दैनिक कर्तव्य तक्ता दिनांक १०/०९/२०२६ · गुरुवार ``` - 10–12px print title; - 8–9px metadata; - lifecycle shown as a small text label, not a large pill; - header height reduced substantially; - repeated on each print sheet only because it is operationally useful. ## Section band Use a narrow section band: ```text 01 दिवसपाळी — ०९:०० ते २१:०० ८२ कर्मचारी ``` - number optional and very small; - title left aligned; - time right aligned; - one 1px rule below; - no rounded container; - count is informational and subtle. ## Row grammar Every staff row should have a predictable form: ```text role / duty label staff display name time / state ``` Example: ```text रायटर पोहवा ६९२ गुंबाडे — पोशि ५६९ पवार बिमा पोशि १२४४ महाले बिमा पोशि २१५७ गुंजाळ ``` Rules: - role labels use `rowspan`; - role labels are not repeated for every person; - staff display name uses compact source form; - full master name remains available in editor/detail view; - time is a small right-side value; - role, name and state remain separate fields; - no inline explanatory prose unless it is source content; - no value is truncated; - two-line wrap is allowed; - avoid one-word orphan lines. ## Staff display For dense chart display: ```text rank + buckle + surname ``` Examples: ```text पोशि ५४२ आहेर पोहवा ६९२ गुंबाडे पोनि सुनिल पवार ``` In the editor/detail panel: ```text Full name: पोहवा ६९२ अनिल बाळु गुंबाडे Rank: HC Buckle: 692 Source/status/history... ``` This gives density without losing identity. ## State display Use text first, color second. ### `रिक्त` ```text रिक्त ``` - dashed underline or dashed empty-seat rule; - amber text; - no filled pill. ### `बंद` ```text बंद · चार्ज → मालेगाव स्टँड ``` - one compact state row; - muted hatch or pale yellow background; - `बंद` never confused with a vacant assignment. ### `बिमा` ```text पोशि १२४४ महाले बिमा ``` - small red text marker; - no large red pill; - remains assignment-level only. --- # 4. Proposed page/section strategy This is **not a recreation of the old six-page format**. It is a new logical grouping that may still print to five or six adaptive sheets when the real data requires it. ## Sheet 1 — Command + daytime deployment ### Top band: command strip Replace large officer cards with a compact command strip: ```text वरिष्ठ पोलीस निरीक्षक: गजेंद्र पाटील रायटर: ... चालक दिवस: ... चालक रात्र: ... ``` Then a compact officer matrix: ```text अधिकारी शाखा/भूमिका आजची नेमणूक पोनि ... क्राईम उपस्थित सपोनि ... तपास ०९–१४ ... ``` This preserves the officer information but avoids four large boxes. ### Main body: three lanes ```text दिवसपाळी मुख्य ठिकाणे | मोबाईल / DB / लॉकअप | कार्यालयीन / विशेष ``` Why three lanes: - the existing four equal columns make day/night columns too narrow; - office/special roles have different density from station deployment; - the chart should not force unrelated rows into equal-height cards. Use a continuous table within each lane, not a card. ### Daytime content Include: - station leadership; - station amaldar; - hazari; - CCTNS; - wireless; - Peter/CR/Delta/DB; - lockup; - special desk/office roles that actually belong to daytime. Do not place all chowki people here if they are shown in the dedicated chowki sheet. Avoid duplicate rendering. ## Sheet 2 — Night deployment + instructions Night data is structurally different from day data. Do not force night instructions into fake staff rows. Use: ```text रात्रपाळी कर्मचारी lanes रात्रपाळी सूचना ``` Left side: - checking officer; - PSO; - hazari; - CCTNS; - wireless; - mobile teams; - DB; - lockup; - night special posts. Right side: - Good Morning Squad; - Ramkund patrol; - statue visits; - chowki rounds; - DB instructions; - app scanning; - establishment closure instructions. Instructions should be compact numbered text blocks, not huge bordered cards. ## Sheet 3 — Chowki command matrix This is the strongest part of the current mock and should remain its own focused sheet. Use a 3×2 grid: ```text काटया मारूती | पंचवटी कारंजा | मालेगाव स्टँड सरदार | फुलेनगर | मेरी ``` Each chowki block: ```text चौकी नाव प्रभारी / वेळ दिवसपाळी रात्रपाळी staff rows staff rows बिमा rows बिमा rows मार्शल line बंद / चार्ज line ``` ### Important improvement Do not put thick borders around each chowki. Instead: - use a thin vertical rule between columns; - use a slightly darker heading underline; - use a very light background only for the heading row; - use whitespace between groups; - use one shared outer grid. A chowki block should feel like a newspaper column, not a dashboard card. ### Marshal handling Keep the current data model: - marshal remains a separate operational post; - display position may fold into its paired chowki; - its own closure/charge state remains explicit; - no BIMA inference. ## Sheet 4 — Leave, other duties, events and notices This should be a flowing multi-column register, not four independent cards. Suggested structure: ```text साप्ताहिक सुट्टी | रजा / सिक | तपास / प्रशिक्षण / प्रतिनियुक्ती | इतर सूचना ``` Use: - category heading once; - people beneath it; - date/time annotations in a narrow secondary column; - no blank card height matching; - columns should flow downward independently; - if one category is longer, it continues naturally beneath the next compatible section rather than leaving empty white space. For notices: - use a full-width notice strip below the lists; - numbered lines; - no card per notice; - group by day/night/source scope; - keep source wording. For 11/09: - event/bandobast should appear as an optional annex band or additional adaptive sheet; - not force Ganpati fields into the ordinary daily chart. ## Sheet 5 — Manpower + change ledger ### Manpower matrix The matrix should remain table-like because it is genuinely tabular. Improvements: - compact two-line column headers; - freeze/shorten only display labels, never data; - use hairline grid; - avoid a large surrounding card; - show source-entered values exactly; - clearly mark derived values separately; - do not “repair” contradictory ME/03 values. ### Change ledger Put it directly below the matrix with only the required columns: ```text क्रमांक | बदल / कारण | नोंद ``` Do not leave a giant empty table area if there are no entries. Show: ```text अचानक बदल नोंद: आज कोणतीही नोंद नाही. ``` and preserve an editor action to add one. ## Sheet 6 — Officer summary + scan schedule + sign-off ### Officer summary Use a two-column table: ```text क्र. | अधिकारी | कर्तव्य ``` The current 15-row summary is inherently compact and should not be turned into individual officer boxes. ### Scan schedule The current hourly scan list should become a time grid: ```text वेळ चौकी कर्मचारी ०९–१० मेरी ... १०–११ मालेगाव ... ... ``` For screen: - allow a compact horizontal time grid if wide enough; - for print, use two side-by-side 6-row tables rather than one tall 12-row table. Example: ```text ०९–१४ १५–२१ ०९–१० ... १५–१६ ... ... १४–१५ ... २०–२१ ... ``` This preserves all 12 rows while reducing vertical waste. ### Sign-off Keep sign-off as a simple bottom rule and three aligned fields. No card. --- # 5. Adaptive pagination strategy Do not hardcode “one logical section equals one physical page.” Use: - logical sections in `ChartDocument`; - content-aware print flow; - continuation only when necessary; - repeated compact section headers when a section continues; - no orphan continuation pages. ### Page-fit rules For every representative real chart: - no page-level horizontal overflow; - no content truncation; - no row loss; - no font below the agreed minimum; - no orphaned section title at page bottom; - no section forced into a tiny unreadable area; - no huge empty region when following content can flow into it. The target is not “fewest pages.” The target is: > **Fewest readable sheets that preserve every source fact.** The old six-page packet may remain six or seven sheets in some cases. That is acceptable if the new grammar is visibly cleaner, more compact and easier to scan. --- # 6. CRUD interaction design The chart should remain visually clean in preview mode. Editing chrome appears only in edit mode. ## Assignment edit Click a staff row → open a right-side inspector/flyout. Inspector: ```text कर्तव्य: काटया मारूती पाळी: दिवसपाळी सध्याची नेमणूक: पोशि ५४२ आहेर [कर्मचारी बदला] [रिक्त करा] [बिमा लागू करा] [वेळ संपादित करा] [नोंद पहा] ``` Staff picker: - search by name/buckle/rank; - current person pinned at top; - list uses compact rank + buckle + surname; - availability warning is informational; - no automatic replacement; - user explicitly selects. ## BIMA Only in the assignment inspector: ```text बिमा: [ ] फक्त या नेमणुकीसाठी ``` Never infer it from duty title, location or notes. ## Location state Click the chowki heading or state line: ```text चौकी: पंचवटी कारंजा पाळी: दिवसपाळी स्थिती: ( ) कार्यरत ( ) बंद चार्ज: [ destination ] ``` Do not expose closure as a person-row status. ## Add row Use contextual `+` only at the end of a logical group: ```text + कर्मचारी + ड्युटी + सूचना ``` The `+` should not appear on every row. ## Add chowki/officer block Keep the existing real persistence behavior, but visually present it as: - a new column/group in the chart; - no fake empty card; - one real vacant slot; - explicit label; - no invented person or timing. ## Label editing Keep the existing per-chart label functionality, but visually: - pencil appears only on hover/focus in edit mode; - no layout reflow; - popover offers: - `फक्त हे`; - `सर्वत्र`; - finalized chart remains immutable. ## Names and free text conversion Future guided conversion: ```text English input ↓ Marathi suggestion ↓ user reviews/edits ↓ explicit Save ``` This must apply only to approved fields and never silently overwrite names or operational text. --- # 7. Design verification before implementation We should not implement blindly. First create a design fixture matrix using real 10/09 data: ### Compare three versions 1. Legacy/reference six-page output. 2. Current compv3 mock with real data. 3. Proposed compact-v4 layout. Measure: - physical sheet count; - printable height used per sheet; - unused whitespace; - nested border count; - repeated labels; - wrapped rows; - longest row height; - page-level overflow; - source rows rendered; - readability at normal zoom; - grayscale distinguishability; - edit-mode layout stability. ### Minimum acceptance targets - 212/212 assignment rows represented; - no page-level horizontal overflow; - no Marathi truncation; - no nested card borders in chart content; - no section title stranded alone at a page bottom; - no large avoidable blank gaps; - no print text smaller than the agreed readability floor; - BIMA/रिक्त/बंद distinguishable without color alone; - screen preview and print use the same document semantics; - edit hover does not move rows or alter geometry. --- # 8. My honest recommendation Do **not** migrate to React or redesign the navbar yet. First, build a **static Compact-v4 design prototype** from the existing 10/09 data using the current renderer data shape, then compare it visually against: - the compv3 mock; - the current root screenshot; - the original 10/09 visual pages. The key redesign is: 1. keep the mock’s logical grouping; 2. remove card treatment; 3. convert officer boxes into a compact command strip; 4. give day, night and chowki content dedicated dense lanes; 5. make leave/notice sections flow independently; 6. convert scan schedule to two compact time grids; 7. use adaptive content-driven pagination; 8. test the layout against full real data before React authoring work. That will answer the most important question first: > Is Compact-v4 genuinely more efficient and readable than the original six-page chart, or merely a prettier mock? Honest assessment of the current mock ### The mock is directionally correct `design/panchavati-compv3.html` is a good starting point because it: - looks like a chart, not a dashboard; - has useful compact grouping; - avoids the old six-page layout; - keeps day/night/chowki/leave/manpower/scan information conceptually separate; - has a calmer visual language; - uses a reasonable dense table grammar; - keeps `रिक्त`, `बंद` and `बिमा` visually distinct. ### But it is not yet proven to be more efficient The screenshot: ```text Current_Screenshots_before_astra\Screenshot_panchavati-compv3_html.png ``` uses sample-sized data. It therefore gives a false impression of how well the layout handles a real day. The screenshot of the current data-backed implementation: ```text Current_Screenshots_before_astra\Screenshot_Current_root_127.0.0.1_3100_charts_2026-09-10.png ``` shows the opposite problem: - too many cards; - excessive repeated borders; - large vertical expansion; - too much dashboard-like framing; - weak grouping of dense real data; - page sections that do not use available horizontal space well. So the honest verdict is: > **Compv3 is a good information-architecture start, but not a finished high-density chart design.** We should preserve its grouping ideas while redesigning its geometry and visual grammar. --- # 2. Core visual strategy The new chart should feel like: > **A compact operational command document made from bands, lanes and disciplined tables — not a dashboard made from cards.** ## Remove from the chart - rounded cards; - shadows; - nested boxes; - double borders; - large empty padding; - decorative KPI tiles; - oversized colored pills; - repeated labels; - full names repeated in every row; - unnecessary icons; - excessive explanatory text; - page-level whitespace created only to make cards equal height. ## Keep - one outer page frame; - thin section rules; - small section headers; - readable dense rows; - subtle color semantics; - compact source-faithful groupings; - explicit operational states; - full data available in the editor/detail panel. ## Border rule Inside the printed chart: - one outer page rule; - one section divider; - hairline internal table rules only where they improve scanning; - no independently bordered card for every office, chowki or officer. A chowki should look like a newspaper/table column, not a UI card. --- # 3. Typography and density The chart needs a deliberately declared scale. ## Print target Approximate starting range: - page title: 12–14px; - section heading: 9.5–11px; - staff row: 8.8–10px; - secondary annotation: 8–8.8px; - table header: 8.5–9.5px. Do not keep shrinking indefinitely. The chart must remain readable when printed and photographed. ## Name strategy In the chart: ```text rank + buckle + surname ``` Examples: ```text पोशि ५४२ आहेर पोहवा ६९२ गुंबाडे पोनि सुनिल पवार ``` In the editor/detail panel: ```text पूर्ण नाव: पोहवा ६९२ अनिल बाळु गुंबाडे हुद्दा: HC बकल: ६९२ ``` This preserves identity without wasting chart width. ## Row rules - Group labels use `rowspan`. - A label appears once per logical group. - Staff names continue below it without repeating the label. - Times use a narrow right-aligned column. - Roles such as `रायटर`, `चालक`, `बिमा` remain separate fields. - Long names may wrap to two lines. - Nothing is truncated. - No isolated one-word line should be produced accidentally. --- # 4. Page and section strategy This is not a recreation of the old six-page chart. It is a new logical arrangement that may still require five or six adaptive print sheets for a large real day. The goal is not the smallest page count. > **The goal is the fewest readable sheets that preserve every fact.** ## Sheet 1 — Command strip and daytime core ### Replace the large officer boxes The current four officer boxes consume too much height and create repeated borders. Use a compact command strip: ```text वरिष्ठ पोलीस निरीक्षक: गजेंद्र पाटील रायटर: ... चालक दिवस: ... चालक रात्र: ... ``` Below that, use a compact officer table only when required: ```text अधिकारी भूमिका/शाखा आजची स्थिती पोनि ... क्राईम उपस्थित सपोनि ... तपास ०९–१४ सपोनि ... प्रशासन उपस्थित ``` No four large cards. ### Main daytime lanes Use three unequal horizontal lanes: ```text दिवसपाळी मुख्य ठिकाणे | मोबाईल / DB / लॉकअप | कार्यालयीन / विशेष ``` They should not be equal width if their content density differs. Likely widths: - main station deployment: 42%; - mobile/DB/lockup: 28%; - office/special: 30%. The important improvement is not just shrinking text. It is allocating width according to content. ### Avoid duplicate chowki data If chowki staff appears in the dedicated chowki sheet, do not repeat all chowki personnel on Sheet 1. Sheet 1 should focus on: - station leadership; - station amaldar; - hazari; - CCTNS; - wireless; - mobile units; - DB; - lockup; - office/special posts. ## Sheet 2 — Night core and instructions Night content is not just a second staff list. It contains directive prose. Use two broad lanes: ```text रात्रपाळी कर्मचारी रात्रपाळी सूचना ``` ### Left lane - checking officer; - night PSO; - hazari; - CCTNS; - wireless; - mobile; - DB; - lockup; - night special posts. ### Right lane - Good Morning Squad; - Ramkund patrol; - statue visits; - chowki rounds; - DB instructions; - app scanning; - establishment closure instructions. Instructions should be: ```text १. गुडमॉर्निंग स्कॉड... २. रामकुंड परिसरात... ३. सर्व बीट मार्शल... ``` Do not render them as fake assignment rows or tall cards. ## Sheet 3 — Chowki command matrix This is the best part of the current mock and should remain focused. Use a 3×2 arrangement: ```text काटया मारूती पंचवटी कारंजा मालेगाव स्टँड सरदार फुलेनगर मेरी ``` Each block should contain: ```text चौकी नाव प्रभारी + वेळ दिवसपाळी | रात्रपाळी staff rows बिमा rows मार्शल/state line ``` ### Visual treatment Remove the heavy individual card look. Use: - one shared outer matrix; - thin internal separators; - lightly tinted heading row; - no shadows; - no rounded corners; - no full border around every sub-column; - whitespace between groups instead of extra boxes. ### Marshal handling Keep the current semantic model: - marshal is a separate operational post; - its display may be folded into the paired chowki; - its `बंद` and `चार्ज` state remains explicit; - BIMA is never inferred. ### Example ```text काटया मारूती चौकी प्रभारी: सपोनि हेमंत मोहिते · ०९–१४ दिवसपाळी रात्रपाळी पोशि ५४२ आहेर पोशि ... पोशि १९९८ वाकचैरे बिमा पोशि ... मार्शल: बंद · चार्ज → मालेगाव ``` The state line should be one compact line that wraps only the destination if necessary. ## Sheet 4 — Leave, other duties, notices Do not use equal-height cards. Use an independently flowing column layout: ```text साप्ताहिक सुट्टी | रजा / सिक | तपास / प्रशिक्षण | इतर ड्युटी ``` Each column flows naturally according to its own row count. ### Row form ```text पोशि ५४२ आहेर ०८ ते १० पोनि ... २८/०८ ते ११/०९ ``` - name on the left; - date/time annotation on the right; - category header once; - no repeated category pill on every row. ### Notices Place notices in a full-width lower band: ```text सूचना व निर्देश १. ... २. ... ३. ... ``` Do not create one card per notice. ### 11/09 event The Ganpati event should become: - a clearly labelled event annex; - an additional adaptive sheet when present; - not a forced section inside the ordinary daily chart. ## Sheet 5 — Manpower and change ledger ### Manpower matrix Keep it as a real matrix, not a card. Improvements: - compact two-line headers; - hairline grid; - values not bolded unnecessarily; - clear distinction between source-entered and derived values; - no automatic reconciliation of `ME`, `03` or contradictory totals; - preserve `..`, blanks and source artifacts exactly where required. ### Change ledger When empty, do not print a huge empty table. Use: ```text अचानक ड्युटी बदल — आज कोणतीही नोंद नाही. ``` When populated, expand into: ```text क्रमांक | बदल / कारण | नोंद ``` ## Sheet 6 — Officer summary, scans and sign-off ### Officer summary The 15-row officer summary should be one compact table: ```text क्र. | अधिकारी | कर्तव्य ``` Do not turn officers into cards here. The command strip already gives the high-level view. ### Scan schedule Use two side-by-side six-row tables: ```text ०९–१५ १५–२१ वेळ | चौकी | कर्मचारी वेळ | चौकी | कर्मचारी ०९–१० ... १५–१६ ... १०–११ ... १६–१७ ... ... १४–१५ ... २०–२१ ... ``` This uses horizontal space instead of producing one tall 12-row block. ### Sign-off Use simple aligned footer fields: ```text तयार करणारे तपासणी अधिकारी मान्यता ``` No footer card. --- # 5. Adaptive pagination The renderer should not assume: ```text one logical section = one physical page ``` Instead: - sections are logical; - physical sheets are content-driven; - a long section may continue; - continuation gets a compact repeated heading; - no orphaned heading; - no blank page created just because a section has a fixed card height. For example: - normal day may render 5 sheets; - a dense day may render 6; - 11/09 with event annex may render 7; - a sparse day should not have huge empty regions just to preserve fixed boxes. This is more honest than promising that every chart always fits the sample mock's page count. --- # 6. CRUD interaction design The chart remains clean in Preview mode. Edit mode adds affordances without changing geometry. ## Assignment editing Click a staff row → open a right-side inspector. ```text कर्तव्य: काटया मारूती पाळी: दिवसपाळी सध्याची नेमणूक: पोशि ५४२ आहेर [कर्मचारी बदला] [रिक्त करा] [बिमा लागू करा] [वेळ संपादित करा] [नोंद पहा] ``` The picker: - searches Marathi name; - searches English name; - searches buckle; - searches rank; - shows current person first; - shows availability as a warning only; - never auto-replaces anyone. ## BIMA Only an explicit assignment field: ```text बिमा: [ ] फक्त या नेमणुकीसाठी ``` Never infer it from: - location; - role; - text; - marshal status; - notes. ## Chowki state Click the chowki header or state line: ```text चौकी: पंचवटी कारंजा पाळी: दिवसपाळी स्थिती: ( ) कार्यरत ( ) बंद चार्ज: [ destination ] ``` `बंद` is a location-state editor, not a staff-row status. ## Adding rows Contextual actions should appear only at meaningful group boundaries: ```text + कर्मचारी + ड्युटी + सूचना + घटना ``` Do not put `+` on every row. ## Label edits Keep the existing real per-chart label behavior: - `फक्त हे`; - `सर्वत्र`; - no geometry shift; - no editing of people or source values through the label editor; - finalized charts remain immutable. --- # 7. Long-lived entities independent of any chart: Staff, Rank, Buckle number, DutyDefinition, Location/Chowki, MarshalPost, Unit, equipment attributes.

### 5.1 Per-chart editable names — ✅ DONE 2026-10-12
**As implemented (differs from the draft below in two ways: no schema/projection change was needed —
`labels`/`labelsAll` sit inside the already-projected `presentation_overrides`, which lands in
`doc.template.overrides`, so FINALIZE snapshots carry their names for free; and each element also
emits `data-override` so the popover knows which scope is live):**
- **Renderer** `makeNames(doc)` → `Names{t,a}`: `t(key,def)` = element override → text-keyed
  override → default; `a(key,def)` emits `data-label` (stable key) + `data-default` (SOURCE text,
  never the override) + `data-override="element|all"`. Wired on **185 elements**: `head.h1/h2`,
  `p1.desk.*`, `box.<label>`(+`.nm`/`.role`), `blk.<key>`(+`.DAY|NIGHT`), `grp.<asnId>`,
  `role.<asnId>`, `sec.*`, `avail.*`, `notice.*`, `mcol.*`, `mrow.*`, `ssum.*`, `chg.h.*`,
  `off.h.*`, `scan.s/h.*`, `signoff.1-3`. NOT rename-able by rule: the date/weekday line (D-rule),
  person names, matrix cell VALUES, state words (बंद/चार्ज).
- **API** `PATCH /api/charts/:date/labels` `{scope:"element"|"all", key?, defaultText?, text}` →
  merged under a row lock; FINALIZED → 409; blank text deletes the entry (back to default);
  160-char cap.
- **UI** edit mode → dotted hover (outline+tint only) → click/Enter → flyer with input +
  फक्त हे / सर्वत्र radios (pre-selected from `data-override`) → PATCH → reload.
- **Verified** browser E2E: element rename, scope=all rename (night desk untouched), blank revert,
  `data-override` round-trip; test `override resolution …` in tests/authoring.test.ts.

#### original design brief (kept for reference)
> "make every table, chart or column name, left rows name editable, just their names, for the user to
> tweak namings as per their likings for that version of the chart."

Scope: **per chart** (never masters, never other dates). UI must offer **both** scopes (user's words:
"There should be an option saying only for this all apply all wide").

- **Storage** — `daily_charts.presentation_overrides` (jsonb, already exists):
  `{ "labels": { "<elementKey>": "<new>" }, "labelsAll": { "<originalText>": "<new>" } }`.
- **Projection** — add `labels`/`labelsAll` to `ChartDocument` (`server/chart-document.ts`, from
  `daily_charts.presentation_overrides`); keeps snapshots self-contained (finalize stores the document).
- **Renderer** — one helper used at every named element:
  `const L = (key, text) => labels[key] ?? labelsAll[text] ?? text;`
  and emit `data-label="<key>" data-label-text="<default text>"` so the UI can address it.
  Sites to wire (in `server/render/chart-html.ts`): `headHtml` h1/h2; `.sec h2`; `deskBlock` titles
  (day/night/office/court); officer box chip + रायटर role th; `.ch-head .nm` (location name);
  `.sub-col-title`; availability section titles + availability block keys; notices title + notice group
  keys; matrix `<th>` labels (template `matrixColumns`) + row keys; shift-summary labels + `<th>`;
  officer-summary/scan/sign-off headings and `<th>`s.
  Suggested key scheme: `head.h1`, `sec.<code>`, `p1.desk.<day|night|office|court>`,
  `p1.box.<label>.chip|role`, `p2.blk.<locationCode>`, `p2.blk.<locationCode>.<SHIFT>.title`,
  `p2.row.<assignmentId>`, `p3.avail.<groupKey>`, `p3.notice.<groupKey>`, `p4.mcol.<key>`,
  `p4.scol.<label>`, `p5.*`, `signoff.*`.
- **API** — `PATCH /api/charts/:date/labels` with `{ scope: "element"|"all", key?, text?, nameMr|null }`
  → merge into `presentation_overrides`; refuse on FINALIZED (409) exactly like the chowki route.
- **UI** — in edit mode, any `[data-label]` gets a dotted hover box; click opens a small popover

  `web/chart-authoring.js`. A blank value clears the override (falls back to the default name).

## Final Agreed Rules

**Officer arrangement**
- Keep the SPI-approved hierarchy:
  1. Senior officer above.
  2. Four subordinate officer blocks arranged horizontally.
  3. Day/night duty areas below.
- Senior officer identity stays on one line: `वपोनि गजेंद्र पाटील ठाणे प्रमुख`.
- Senior support roles use dynamic horizontal columns: writer, driver, RTPC, operator.
- Driver, RTPC, and operator may have compact day/night subdivisions. Writer does not unless source data requires it.
- Officer blocks start directly with the officer name and branch. No separate `अधिकारी १`, `अधिकारी २` heading row.
- Show only source-backed officer relationships. Never invent writer, RTPC, operator, or other assignments.
- Empty/unsupported rows or groups may be hidden individually to save space.
- Alignment controls are approved for editable elements: left, centered, right, top, middle, bottom, plus compact/hidden behavior.

**Headers and navigation**
- Use a persistent application navbar/header across all pages.
- Main header contains identity and navigation only. It must not contain `DRAFT`, `FINALIZED`, Edit, Finalize, or Print actions.
- Avoid duplicated English and Marathi labels. The navbar language toggle controls UI labels.
- The printed chart header is one centered line:

  `नाशिक शहर पोलीस आयुक्तालय   दैनिक कर्तव्य वाटप   १० सप्टेंबर २०२६, गुरुवार`

- Do not add explanatory labels such as `दिनांक` or `वार`, decorative dots, em dashes, large title rows, or excessive empty header space.
- Chart-specific status and actions belong in a compact toolbar below the persistent header.
- Remove emoji-style action labels and redundant bilingual text.

**Chart structure and pagination**
- Keep day and night side-by-side where their first three logical groupings correspond.
- Do not model every staff member as a large isolated row.
- Move office, clerical, court, summons, warrant, and special-duty content away from Page 1, primarily to the next sheet.
- Use compact grouped tables with thin rules, light heading bands, no card shadows, and no nested rounded cards.
- Target pagination:
  - Normal date: 5–6 sheets.
  - Dense/event date: 6–7 sheets.
  - 10/09 target: no more than 6 sheets if readable.
  - 11/09 with event annex: no more than 7 sheets.
- Preserve all authoritative information, Marathi wrapping, and assignment count. Compactness must come from grouping and removing repetition, not tiny unreadable text.

**Must not be embedded or recreated**
- Do not recreate the old Kushal standardized chart as the active design target.
- Do not recreate the old legacy six-page layout merely for familiarity. It may appear only as Reference/WIP/Coming Soon.
- Do not put all office/court/special content back onto Page 1.
- Do not use one-staff-per-large-row treatment.
- Do not use fake officer/operator/RTPC data.
- Do not use heavy literal boxes from the rough diagrams; those diagrams describe hierarchy only.
- Do not allow arbitrary persisted HTML, CSS, or JavaScript presentation overrides. The later implementation explicitly restricts controls to validated alignment, visibility, and compactness values.

**CRUD behavior**
- Clicking an assignment opens a centered, viewport-safe popup/flyout while preserving the clicked chart context.
- It must support, without navigating to a separate master-data page:
  - Editing the current staff master record.
  - Selecting an existing staff member from searchable master data.
  - Creating a new staff member and assigning them immediately.
  - Clearing the assignment.
  - Assignment-specific fields such as time, BIMA, and notes.
- Master fields and assignment fields must remain visibly separate.
- The popup should scroll internally only when needed, support Escape and outside click, show success/failure clearly, return to the same slot after saving, and avoid chart reflow behind it.
- No automatic replacement or autonomous staffing decisions.

**Lifecycle**
- The user initially suggested switching finalized charts directly back to draft.
- The later agreed rule reverses that: finalized charts remain immutable. “Start amendment” creates a new draft version; the original finalized chart is preserved.
- The persistent navbar must not carry chart lifecycle state.

**Explicit approvals and implementation status**
- The user explicitly approved the compact, space-saving direction and said to proceed with implementation at [`mega.txt`](mega.txt#L3007).
- Earlier proposals for a compact command strip/matrix, two-line senior officer block, and different day/night model were rejected or superseded.
- The later final interpretation confirms the persistent header, one-line senior officer, dynamic support columns, four horizontal officer blocks, adaptive pagination, and CRUD popup at [`mega.txt`](mega.txt#L3365).

modeInstructions.content:
You are a PLANNING AGENT, pairing with the user to create a detailed, actionable plan.

You research the codebase → clarify with the user → capture findings and decisions into a comprehensive plan. This iterative approach catches edge cases and non-obvious requirements BEFORE implementation begins.

Your SOLE responsibility is planning. NEVER start implementation.

**Current plan**: `/memories/session/plan.md` - update using #tool:vscode/memory .

<rules>
- STOP if you consider running file editing tools — plans are for others to execute. The only write tool you have is #tool:vscode/memory for persisting plans.
- Use #tool:vscode/askQuestions freely to clarify requirements — don't make large assumptions
- Present a well-researched plan with loose ends tied BEFORE implementation
</rules>

<workflow>
Cycle through these phases based on user input. This is iterative, not linear. If the user task is highly ambiguous, do only *Discovery* to outline a draft plan, then move on to alignment before fleshing out the full plan.

## 1. Discovery

Run the *Explore* subagent to gather context, analogous existing features to use as implementation templates, and potential blockers or ambiguities. When the task spans multiple independent areas (e.g., frontend + backend, different features, separate repos), launch **2-3 *Explore* subagents in parallel** — one per area — to speed up discovery.

Update the plan with your findings.

## 2. Alignment

If research reveals major ambiguities or if you need to validate assumptions:
- Use #tool:vscode/askQuestions to clarify intent with the user.
- Surface discovered technical constraints or alternative approaches
- If answers significantly change the scope, loop back to **Discovery**

## 3. Design

Once context is clear, draft a comprehensive implementation plan.

The plan should reflect:
- Structured concise enough to be scannable and detailed enough for effective execution
- Step-by-step implementation with explicit dependencies — mark which steps can run in parallel vs. which block on prior steps
- For plans with many steps, group into named phases that are each independently verifiable
- Verification steps for validating the implementation, both automated and manual
- Critical architecture to reuse or use as reference — reference specific functions, types, or patterns, not just file names
- Critical files to be modified (with full paths)
- Explicit scope boundaries — what's included and what's deliberately excluded
- Reference decisions from the discussion
- Leave no ambiguity

Save the comprehensive plan document to `/memories/session/plan.md` via #tool:vscode/memory, then show the scannable plan to the user for review. You MUST show plan to the user, as the plan file is for persistence only, not a substitute for showing it to the user.

## 4. Refinement

On user input after showing the plan:
- Changes requested → revise and present updated plan. Update `/memories/session/plan.md` to keep the documented plan in sync
- Questions asked → clarify, or use #tool:vscode/askQuestions for follow-ups
- Alternatives wanted → loop back to **Discovery** with new subagent
- Approval given → acknowledge, the user can now use handoff buttons

Keep iterating until explicit approval or handoff.
</workflow>

<plan_style_guide>
```markdown
## Plan: {Title (2-10 words)}

{TL;DR - what, why, and how (your recommended approach).}

**Steps**
1. {Implementation step-by-step — note dependency ("*depends on N*") or parallelism ("*parallel with step N*") when applicable}
2. {For plans with 5+ steps, group steps into named phases with enough detail to be independently actionable}

**Relevant files**
- `{full/path/to/file}` — {what to modify or reuse, referencing specific functions/patterns}

**Verification**
1. {Verification steps for validating the implementation (**Specific** tasks, tests, commands, MCP tools, etc; not generic statements)}

**Decisions** (if applicable)
- {Decision, assumptions, and includes/excluded scope}

**Further Considerations** (if applicable, 1-3 items)
1. {Clarifying question with recommendation. Option A / Option B / Option C}
2. {…}
```

Rules:
- NO code blocks — describe changes, link to files and specific symbols/functions
- NO blocking questions at the end — ask during workflow via #tool:vscode/askQuestions
- The plan MUST be presented to the user, don't just mention the plan file.
</plan_style_guide>

**Headers and navigation**
- Use a persistent application navbar/header across all pages.
- Main header contains identity and navigation only. It must not contain `DRAFT`, `FINALIZED`, Edit, Finalize, or Print actions.
- Avoid duplicated English and Marathi labels. The navbar language toggle controls UI labels.
- The printed chart header is one centered line:

  `नाशिक शहर पोलीस आयुक्तालय   दैनिक कर्तव्य वाटप   १० सप्टेंबर २०२६, गुरुवार`

- Do not add explanatory labels such as `दिनांक` or `वार`, decorative dots, em dashes, large title rows, or excessive empty header space.
- Chart-specific status and actions belong in a compact toolbar below the persistent header.
- Remove emoji-style action labels and redundant bilingual text.

**Chart structure and pagination**
- Keep day and night side-by-side where their first three logical groupings correspond.
- Do not model every staff member as a large isolated row.
- Move office, clerical, court, summons, warrant, and special-duty content away from Page 1, primarily to the next sheet.
- Use compact grouped tables with thin rules, light heading bands, no card shadows, and no nested rounded cards.
- Target pagination:
  - Normal date: 5–6 sheets.
  - Dense/event date: 6–7 sheets.
  - 10/09 target: no more than 6 sheets if readable.
  - 11/09 with event annex: no more than 7 sheets.
- Preserve all authoritative information, Marathi wrapping, and assignment count. Compactness must come from grouping and removing repetition, not tiny unreadable text.

**Must not be embedded or recreated**
- Do not recreate the old Kushal standardized chart as the active design target.
- Do not recreate the old legacy six-page layout merely for familiarity. It may appear only as Reference/WIP/Coming Soon.
- Do not put all office/court/special content back onto Page 1.
- Do not use one-staff-per-large-row treatment.
- Do not use fake officer/operator/RTPC data.
- Do not use heavy literal boxes from the rough diagrams; those diagrams describe hierarchy only.
- Do not allow arbitrary persisted HTML, CSS, or JavaScript presentation overrides. The later implementation explicitly restricts controls to validated alignment, visibility, and compactness values.

**CRUD behavior**
- Clicking an assignment opens a centered, viewport-safe popup/flyout while preserving the clicked chart context.
- It must support, without navigating to a separate master-data page:
  - Editing the current staff master record.
  - Selecting an existing staff member from searchable master data.
  - Creating a new staff member and assigning them immediately.
  - Clearing the assignment.
  - Assignment-specific fields such as time, BIMA, and notes.
- Master fields and assignment fields must remain visibly separate.
- The popup should scroll internally only when needed, support Escape and outside click, show success/failure clearly, return to the same slot after saving, and avoid chart reflow behind it.
- No automatic replacement or autonomous staffing decisions.

**Lifecycle**
- The user initially suggested switching finalized charts directly back to draft.
- The later agreed rule reverses that: finalized charts remain immutable. “Start amendment” creates a new draft version; the original finalized chart is preserved.
- The persistent navbar must not carry chart lifecycle state.

**Explicit approvals and implementation status**
- The user explicitly approved the compact, space-saving direction and said to proceed with implementation at [`mega.txt`](mega.txt#L3007).
- Earlier proposals for a compact command strip/matrix, two-line senior officer block, and different day/night model were rejected or superseded.
- The later final interpretation confirms the persistent header, one-line senior officer, dynamic support columns, four horizontal officer blocks, adaptive pagination, and CRUD popup at [`mega.txt`](mega.txt#L3365).
- The file’s later implementation report says presentation controls were implemented server-side and verified, but the remaining todo still calls for a React authoring vertical slice. This is a scope/status inconsistency: the approval allowed React or HTML, while the reported work changed the print renderer and did not complete the React slice.

## 0. What this project is, in one paragraph
A web app for Panchavati Police Station, Nashik City, that replaces the old paper/DOCX daily duty chart
workflow (legacy Kruti Dev 714 Marathi, manually prepared, photographed, and sent on WhatsApp) with a
digitized, editable, searchable system. One station for now, one clerk user for now. Marathi-first,
The product has two chart formats in the team's thinking:

2. The **new compact chart** (`design/panchavati-compv3.html` + `design/compv3.css`) — the approved visual
baseline and the primary implementation target.
The long-term North Star (from Kushal's notes) is: generate tomorrow's chart, edit same-day, finalize and
preserve immutable history, PDF export per chart/page, historical search, and eventually GOWA/WhatsApp
dispatch. This session's implementation focus was the new compact chart and its editing chrome.
- **You (Kushal):** owner/operator. Non-technical daily users are clerks and 12th-pass staff; UI must be
friendly for them. Marathi priority; English toggle acceptable.
- **Arjish:** built a separate, further-along React/Vite repo. Source of the **header design** we ported.

English input and auto-converted to Marathi. Worth reusing for the English→Marathi input idea, but only
as a guided conversion the user can see and edit — never silent overwrites.
- **SPI sir:** rejected Kushal's earlier standardized single-page "too long / scrolling" chart; preferred
the original 6-page Panchavati layout. That critique is why the team studied the first 3 pages and built
`design/panchavati-compv3.html` as a mock of that denser layout.

## 4. The data model (what exists today, in this repo)

existing override shape — reuse it, do not invent new top-level tables for per-chart UI names.

This is why the pseudo-login buckle field is shown conditionally.
- `template_versions` — the template system; marshal/desk folding config is **template display config**, not data:
- `रिक्त` = an existing duty slot with no person.
- `बंद` = a location/chowki operationally closed for that shift; its charge-transfer info is separate.
- `बिमा` = a per-person assignment qualifier; never infer it by parsing notes.
- `प्रभारी` = person in charge of a chowki block.
- `चार्ज` = the transfer/destination associated with a closure.
- A chowki and its neighbouring marshal post can have different operational states. Model them separately.
- Canonical spellings: बिमा (not विमा), पोशि (not पोषि), काळाराम मंदीर (long ी, not मंदिर).
`CCTNS`, `Dial 112 MERS`, `DB`, `MERS`, rank codes, `TOTAL`, `Office`, `ME`, and other source English terms
unless an approved rule establishes a Marathi equivalent. Never guess expansions.
1. **Original source files are authoritative.** Original DOCX, original PDFs, unmodified PNG/visual references.
2. **Semantic extractions and OCR are aids, not authority.** They can be wrong. The team observed this directly:
the semantic extraction wrongly used `काळाराम मंदिर` (short ि) where the Excel reconstruction cell text and the
semantic 10.md lines 37/87 both actually carry the long ी form `काळाराम मंदीर`.
3. **When sources disagree, record the discrepancy and verify against the original.** Do not guess, merge similar
names, or infer relationships from nearby text.
4. **Never silently invent a person, rank, duty, closure, replacement, or police procedure.**
5. **Do not parse `remarks_mr`/note text for machine meaning.** BIMA, closure, charge, रिक्त are explicit fields.
6. **Finalized chart = immutable snapshot.** Amendment = new version. Copy-previous never modifies the source chart.
7. **No police operational data leaves the machine.** No external AI/API calls with chart data, no cloud services
9. **Never edit an applied migration; add a new one.**
